newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB and Channel 5 to explore cooperation.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB and Channel 5 to explore cooperation.

text.p: Satellite broadcaster BSkyB and Channel 5, the UK's new terrestrial television station, are to examine the possibilty of cooperating on certain ventures, David Elstein said on Friday.
Elstein, now head of programming at BSkyB, is joining Channel 5 Broadcasting as Chief Executive Officer. He will begin work in his new job on September 16.
He said BSkyB chief executive Sam Chisholm "can see a lot of opportunities for cooperation between BSkyB and Channel 5".
Sports rights and marketing are two areas for possible cooperation, Elstein told reporters.
But he added he would have to weigh up the pros and cons of cooperation from his new position at Channel 5.
Channel 5 will launch in January 1997. Its shareholders are Pearson, United News & Media, Luxembourg broadcaster CLT and U.S. investment group Warburg Pincus.
"Channel 5 has a clean sheet of paper to work with. We know where gaps in the advertising market are," Elstein said.
He confirmed that Channel 5's annual programming budget would be 100-110 million stg, several times smaller than that of the ITV (Channel 3) network.
Channel 5, which will reach around 75 percent of households at launch, is in the process of retuning video recorders nationwide to avoid interference from its signal.
The retuning exercise will cost around 100 million stg.
Elstein, who was approached for the Channel 5 job two weeks ago, denied he was a trouble-shooter brought in to sort out problems ahead of the launch.
"I wouldn't have come if I thought there were substantial problems," he said.
